next_mission_recommendation.mission_title: Harden Stage Gate: Fix CLI Logic Bug and Add Gemini/Multi-Provider Support
next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: Fix the identified stage gate vulnerabilities: (1) Fix get_disallowed_tools_for_cli() in init_guard.py to use the complementary-set logic for PLANNING instead of the blocked_tools early-return — this ensures Write/Edit/Bash are blocked at CLI Layer 1 for PLANNING, not just at Layer 2; (2) Copy stage_gate_hook.py into the repository at .claude/hooks/ and update settings.json to reference the repo-relative path, ensuring the hook deploys with the codebase; (3) Add Bash restrictions to stage_gate_hook.py for ANALYZING and CYCLE_END stages; (4) Change the fail-open default (BUILDING) in stage_gate_hook.py to fail-closed (COMPLETE) or at minimum ANALYZING; (5) Add provider-agnostic gate enforcement for Gemini/Codex by injecting hard-stop instructions into their system prompts with structured output validation. Each fix must be validated with functional end-to-end tests that verify a PLANNING-stage agent cannot write .py files even if it tries.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The current stage gate system has a single point of failure: if stage_gate_hook.py is absent or the mission.json is unreadable, PLANNING-stage code writing is completely unblocked. The CLI Layer 1 gap (blocked_tools preempting allowed_tools branch) means PLANNING only blocks NotebookEdit at the primary enforcement layer. Hardening this with 5 targeted fixes closes concrete security gaps, ensures multi-provider parity, and makes the gate system resilient to deployment and filesystem failures. This directly addresses the original bug report and prevents recurrence.

final_report.summary: Investigated the AtlasForge stage lockout / tool gate system to determine whether PLANNING stage properly restricts code writing, testing, and state-modifying operations. Found a two-layer enforcement architecture: Layer 1 uses Claude's --disallowedTools CLI flag (via atlasforge_conductor.py + init_guard.py), and Layer 2 uses a PreToolUse hook (stage_gate_hook.py) registered in .claude/settings.json. The PLANNING gate IS enforced via Layer 2 — the hook blocks .py/.js/.ts writes and blocks destructive Bash commands. However, a critical design gap was found: Layer 1 (--disallowedTools) for PLANNING only blocks NotebookEdit (due to a logic branch bug in get_disallowed_tools_for_cli), meaning Write/Edit/Bash are NOT blocked at the CLI level for PLANNING and rely entirely on Layer 2. If the hook is absent, fails, or is bypassed, PLANNING-stage code writing is unblocked. Additional gaps identified: Gemini/Codex providers have zero Layer 1 gate enforcement, the hook defaults to BUILDING (least restrictive) on mission.json parse failure, and the hook file is not version-controlled in the repository.
key_achievements: Fully mapped the two-layer stage gate architecture (CLI --disallowedTools + PreToolUse hook)

Identified the root cause of the observed bug: get_disallowed_tools_for_cli() uses blocked_tools branch for PLANNING (only NotebookEdit), never reaching the allowed_tools complementary-set branch that would block Write/Edit/Bash at CLI level
Confirmed Layer 2 (stage_gate_hook.py) IS working correctly: blocks .py/.js/.ts writes and destructive bash during PLANNING
Documented 7 specific gaps/vulnerabilities in the gate system with file paths and line numbers
Confirmed the hook is properly registered in .claude/settings.json PreToolUse matchers for Write, Edit, and Bash
challenges_overcome: Traced the full call chain from conductor invocation to hook execution across 5+ files
Identified why the allowed_tools branch in get_disallowed_tools_for_cli is dead code for PLANNING (blocked_tools branch preempts it)
Distinguished between cosmetic gaps (preview command bug) and security-relevant gaps (Gemini/Codex no Layer 1, fail-open default)
lessons_learned: The PLANNING stage gate relies critically on stage_gate_hook.py being present at the user-level hooks path — if that file is missing, Layer 2 silently fails and PLANNING has no write restrictions

The get_disallowed_tools_for_cli() logic has a design flaw: for stages with both allowed_tools and blocked_tools set, the blocked_tools branch always wins, skipping the more comprehensive allowed_tools computation

Bash restrictions in stage_gate_hook.py only apply to PLANNING — ANALYZING and CYCLE_END stages have no Bash restrictions in Layer 2, relying solely on Layer 1 (which also doesn't block Bash for ANALYZING/CYCLE_END for Claude)
Gemini and Codex providers have no programmatic gate enforcement — only advisory text in system prompts
The hook's fail-open default (return BUILDING on parse failure) prioritizes uptime over security — a deliberate trade-off but worth documenting
Stage gate hook should be version-controlled in the repository (.claude/hooks/) not just at user-level to ensure it deploys with the codebase
